title: 2026-0122 Provision & Support for BMD OPSLOOP Voice Services (CTS) - FRI 21 Aug
description: 1. BIDDING INSTRUCTIONS Technical Proposal Bidders shall submit a proposal clearly providing the following information: a: The proposed approach to address the required scope of work and the defined deliverables (maximum 10 pages, A4 size). The proposed approach should address the minimum: Sufficient details to allow assessment of the bidders understanding of the requirements. Previous similar experience. Relevant experience of the proposed team members. b: CVs of the assigned resource(s) for the project, and related attestations. It is up to the bidder to propose the size of the team that executes the work and produces the deliverables in the time line allocated. The Purchaser may accommodate a reasonable number of personnel at the current facilities. The CVs shall clearly distinguish if the proposal is for Key Personnel or not. Deadline Date: Friday 21 August 2026 Requirement: Provision and On-Going Support for BMD OPSLOOP Voice Services Location: 100% onsite in Mons, BEL Period of Performance: 2026 BASE: From September 1, 2026 (tentative) to December 31, 2026, with possibility to exercise the following options: 2027 Option: January 1, 2027 until December 31, 2027. 2028 Option: January 1, 2028 until December 31, 2028. Required Security Clearance: NATO COSMIC TOP SECRET (NATO SECRET security clearance is accepted with CTS in progress – deadline to have CTS in place by end of October 2026). Special Terms and Conditions: Statement of Work 1. PURPOSE The purpose of this Statement of Work (SoW) is to define the services for BMD OPSLOOP Voice services in NCI Agency Mons, Belgium. The NCI Agency (hereinafter referred to as the “Purchaser”) seeks a qualified Contractor to provide continuous BMD OPSLOOP Voice services in support of Purchaser personnel based in Mons, Belgium, as well as personnel on official duty at that location. 2. OBJECTIVES The objective of this role is to provide first level support for issues related to BMD OPSLOOP Voice Services and to ensure the optimal performance, security, and reliability of BMD OPSLOOP Voice services. The Contractor shall also provide end-user support, including technical assistance and user guidance where required. The overall objective is to improve user satisfaction, reduce support response times, and enhance the quality and efficiency of IT service delivery. During the performance of the contract, the Contractor shall operate as an integral part of the Purchaser’s NATO Digital Workplace Centre (NDWC), Shared Workspace Group (SWG), delivering on-site BMD OPSLOOP Voice services support. With this SoW, the Purchaser aims to achieve the following objectives: Leverage industry expertise and best practices in installation, configuration, monitoring and daily operation of commercial off the shelf (COTS) technologies and software in the collaboration area. Ensure that BMD OPSLOOP Voice services are functional and fully operational. Perform first-line troubleshooting and escalate issues as required and maintain incident records and operational logs. Support installation of standard BMD OPSLOOP Voice Systems. Provide user assistance before, during, and after meetings. Additional support may be requested to augment the baseline staff for large conferences, VIP meetings, or high-visibility events. 3. INTRODUCTION NATO Digital Workplace Centre (NDWC), part of NCI Agency, provides simple yet innovative solutions that underpin the Digital Transformation of NATO by providing a feature-rich Digital Workplace, which enables NATO staff members to connect, communicate, and collaborate. Shared Workspace service area delivers the following user-facing services to NATO Commands, NATO Force structure and Nations in all 32 Allied Nations: Printing, scanning and copying services, client frontend provisioning, management, operation and lifecycle across multiple separate networks of different classifications. Voice and Video conferencing server backend and frontend devices and rooms, maintenance, management, operation and troubleshooting across multiple separate networks of different classifications. AV/VTC service is designed to give value-added auditory and visual experience to the customers and users while doing their consultation sessions or briefings using the latest technology available. The services integrate with other services and enable NATO-specific functional applications higher up the software stack. Through several on-going streams of work in Q4’24 and onwards, the services are rapidly evolving from using fully on-premise to a mixture of on-premise and public cloud technologies. 4. PURCHASER SUPPORT STRUCTURE The Purchaser support structure is organized into three levels: Level 1 (L1): Centralized Service Desk providing virtual first-line support. Level 2 (L2): On-site technical support, including touch-labor and specialized support provided by the CIS Support Unit or IT Service Kiosk. Level 3 (L3): Centralized engineering support provided by specialist technical teams. a. Deliverables The principal deliverable of this Statement of Work (SoW) is the provision and continuous delivery of the BMD OPSLOOP Voice Service (hereinafter referred to as the “Service”). The Contractor shall: i. BMD OPSLOOP Voice Implementation Provide first level of support to end users for daily business. Ensure that BMD OPSLOOP Voice services are functional and fully operational. Perform first-line troubleshooting, conduct daily preventive readiness checks of BMD OPSLOOP Voice systems, escalate issues as required and maintain incident records and operational logs. Support the installation of standard BMD OPSLOOP Voice Systems. KPI: Service availability: Measurement and target: ≥99.5% availability during agreed operational/service hours, excluding approved maintenance and external dependencies. Acceptance criteria: Availability report demonstrates achievement of target; all exclusions are documented and approved. Evidence: Monitoring report, outage records, maintenance calendar. KPI: Daily readiness checks: Measurement and target: 100% of scheduled checks completed; ≥98% completed within the agreed daily time window. Acceptance criteria: Checklist completed for every scheduled operational day; exceptions documented, actioned and escalated. Evidence: Signed/electronic checklists, operational logs. KPI: First-line response: Measurement and target: ≥95% of incidents acknowledged within the applicable SLA; 100% of critical incidents acknowledged within the critical-incident SLA. Acceptance criteria: Service-management records contain timestamps, categorisation, actions and status. Evidence: Incident records and SLA report. KPI: First-line resolution: Measurement and target: ≥80% of incidents within the agreed first-line scope resolved without unnecessary escalation. Acceptance criteria: Resolution rate achieved; unresolved incidents correctly escalated with diagnostic evidence. Evidence: Incident and escalation records. KPI: Escalation timeliness: Measurement and target: ≥95% of issues outside first-line scope escalated within the agreed SLA; 100% of critical issues escalated immediately in accordance with procedures. Acceptance criteria: Escalations include impact, priority, troubleshooting performed and supporting logs. Evidence: Tickets, escalation notices, operational logs. KPI: Record completeness: Measurement and target: ≥98% of incidents and operational events recorded accurately; 100% of critical incidents fully documented. Acceptance criteria: Mandatory fields completed, including cause/symptoms, actions, timestamps, affected configuration items and resolution. Evidence: Incident-record quality sample. KPI: Standard installation success: Measurement and target: ≥95% of installations accepted at first verification; 100% supported by installation and test records. Acceptance criteria: Installation follows approved baseline; functional test passed; configuration and asset records updated. Evidence: Installation checklist, test results, configuration records. KPI: User support satisfaction: Measurement and target: ≥85% positive satisfaction or agreed equivalent score, subject to a representative response level. Acceptance criteria: Survey results meet target; material complaints are addressed through corrective actions. Evidence: Survey results and action log. The deliverable is accepted when: The agreed support coverage was provided throughout the period. Availability and readiness-check targets were achieved. Incidents were handled, documented and escalated according to approved procedures and SLAs. Standard installations passed functional and configuration verification. No unresolved critical failure attributable to the contractor remains at the acceptance date, unless an approved corrective-action plan exists. ii. Maintenance Preventive maintenance, readiness checks, and escalation of complex issues. Monitor BMD OPSLOOP Voice systems availability, reliability, and performance. Analyze incident service request, and fault trends to identify recurring issues and improvement opportunities. KPI: Preventive-maintenance completion: Measurement and target: 100% of scheduled preventive-maintenance activities completed; ≥95% completed by the planned date. Acceptance criteria: Maintenance tasks completed against the approved schedule; deferrals formally authorised. Evidence: Maintenance schedule, work orders and checklists. KPI: Post-maintenance functionality: Measurement and target: 100% of maintained systems pass post-maintenance functional and readiness testing. Acceptance criteria: Test results demonstrate restoration to the approved operational baseline. Evidence: Test records and readiness confirmation. KPI: System availability: Measurement and target: ≥99.5% during agreed service hours, excluding approved maintenance and accepted dependencies. Acceptance criteria: Availability report reconciles monitoring data with incident and maintenance records. Evidence: Monitoring and availability reports. KPI: Reliability: Measurement and target: No deterioration against the agreed baseline; target reduction of ≥10% in recurring service-affecting faults where sufficient baseline data exists. Acceptance criteria: Reliability trend is stable or improving; adverse trends have documented corrective actions. Evidence: MTBF/fault-frequency trend report. KPI: Performance compliance: Measurement and target: ≥95% of monitored components remain within agreed performance thresholds. Acceptance criteria: Threshold breaches are recorded, investigated and resolved or covered by an approved action plan. Evidence: Performance dashboard and alert records. KPI: Maintenance-related incidents: Measurement and target: No critical incident caused by unauthorised or incorrectly performed maintenance. Acceptance criteria: All changes traceable to approved procedures; any maintenance-induced issue has completed root-cause analysis. Evidence: Change, incident and RCA records. KPI: Trend analysis: Measurement and target: Monthly or Work Package-period analysis covering 100% of critical/high incidents and statistically significant recurring faults. Acceptance criteria: Report identifies recurring issues, causes, operational impact, priorities and recommended actions. Evidence: Trend-analysis report. KPI: Corrective-action closure: Measurement and target: ≥90% of agreed maintenance actions completed by their due dates. Acceptance criteria: Overdue actions have approved revised dates and documented justification. Evidence: Corrective-action tracker. KPI: Complex-issue escalation: Measurement and target: ≥95% escalated within the applicable SLA with complete technical information. Acceptance criteria: Receiving support level confirms sufficient diagnostic evidence was provided. Evidence: Escalation records and ticket audit. The maintenance deliverable is accepted when: All scheduled maintenance and readiness checks were completed or formally deferred. Maintained systems passed post-maintenance testing. Availability, reliability and performance results met the applicable targets. Recurring faults were analysed and improvement actions proposed. Maintenance, incident, problem and escalation records are complete and traceable. Continual Service Improvement Proactive, structured and measurable continual approach ensuring BMD OPSLOOP Voice services evolve in line with the Agency’s needs while maintaining service stability and compliance. Continuously improve the quality and efficiency of BMD OPSLOOP Voice services by monitoring and maintaining a healthy frontend environment, thus reducing the need for support. Identify and provide opportunities for continuous service improvements. KPI: CSI opportunity identification: Measurement and target: Minimum number established per Work Package — recommended: at least 2 substantiated opportunities per quarter. Acceptance criteria: Each opportunity includes problem statement, evidence, expected benefit, risk, effort, owner and priority. Evidence: CSI register and improvement proposals. KPI: CSI assessment timeliness: Measurement and target: 100% of identified opportunities assessed within 20 working days or the Work Package timescale. Acceptance criteria: Opportunities are accepted, rejected, deferred or referred for approval with documented rationale. Evidence: CSI decision log. KPI: Approved improvement delivery: Measurement and target: ≥90% of approved actions completed by the agreed due date. Acceptance criteria: Implementation and validation evidence provided; delays formally approved. Evidence: Improvement plan and completion records. KPI: Measurable service benefit: Measurement and target: ≥80% of implemented improvements achieve their agreed success measure within the evaluation period. Acceptance criteria: Before-and-after results demonstrate the anticipated benefit or contain documented lessons learned. Evidence: Benefits-realisation report. KPI: Support-demand reduction: Measurement and target: Target ≥10% reduction in avoidable/repetitive incidents against the agreed baseline, where statistically valid. Acceptance criteria: Reduction demonstrated using comparable periods, volumes and incident classifications. Evidence: Incident trend and baseline comparison. KPI: Frontend environment health: Measurement and target: ≥95% compliance with agreed health thresholds; no unresolved critical health finding beyond its approved due date. Acceptance criteria: Monitoring shows stable or improving health; threshold breaches have corrective actions. Evidence: Health dashboard and action register. KPI: Service stability after improvement: Measurement and target: 100% of changes implemented through approved change processes; no unmitigated critical incident caused by an improvement. Acceptance criteria: Change validation completed and rollback arrangements evidenced where applicable. Evidence: Change records, validation and post-implementation review. KPI: Compliance preservation: Measurement and target: 100% of implemented improvements comply with applicable security, configuration, documentation and operational requirements. Acceptance criteria: Required reviews and approvals obtained; documentation and configuration baselines updated. Evidence: Compliance checklist and approval records. KPI: Stakeholder acceptance: Measurement and target: ≥85% of sampled stakeholders confirm that delivered improvements provide the intended operational benefit. Acceptance criteria: Feedback collected after implementation and material concerns actioned. Evidence: Feedback and acceptance records. The CSI deliverable is accepted when: A structured CSI register was maintained. Improvement opportunities were evidence-based, prioritised and assessed. Approved improvements were implemented through the appropriate governance and change processes. Benefits were measured against an agreed baseline. Service stability, security and compliance were preserved. Documentation, monitoring thresholds and operational procedures were updated as necessary. Activities and tasks mentioned above will either have combinations or a single focus based on the requirements of the organization at each Work Package. 5. PAYMENT SCHEDULE 2026 BASE performance Deliverable 01: Provision and on-going delivery of BMD OPSLOOP Voice Services. Payment Milestones: Monthly, upon completion of monthly services in accordance with the performance indicators and service levels defined above, including SLA compliance, ticket resolution, system availability, security compliance, reporting, and user support/training activities. 2027, 2028 OPTIONAL performance Deliverable 01: Provision and on-going delivery of BMD OPSLOOP Voice Services. Quantity: Max. 12 Work Packages. Payment Milestones: Monthly, upon completion of monthly services in accordance with the performance indicators and service levels defined above, including SLA compliance, ticket resolution, system availability, security compliance, reporting, and user support/training activities. Since each Work Package may contain one, several, or all three service areas, the payment weighting should be established in the Work Package Order before execution. a. Work Package payment model Each Work Package defines its applicable service areas and allocates 100% of its value accordingly. Operations-focused: 60% Implementation and operations, 30% Maintenance, 10% CSI. Balanced service support: 45% Implementation and operations, 35% Maintenance, 20% CSI. Maintenance-focused: 25% Implementation and operations, 60% Maintenance, 15% CSI. Improvement-focused: 25% Implementation and operations, 25% Maintenance, 50% CSI. Single-focus Work Package: 100% to the applicable area. Within each service area, payment is divided as follows: Implementation and operations payment allocation Availability and operational readiness: 35%. Incident response, resolution and escalation: 30%. Operational records and reporting: 15%. Standard installations and verification: 15%. User satisfaction and service quality: 5%. Total: 100%. Maintenance payment allocation Preventive maintenance and readiness checks: 30%. Availability, reliability and performance: 30%. Post-maintenance testing and configuration control: 15%. Incident/fault trend analysis: 15%. Corrective-action closure and reporting: 10%. Total: 100%. CSI payment allocation CSI register and opportunity assessment: 20%. Approved improvement implementation: 35%. Measured benefits and support-demand reduction: 25%. Stability, compliance and change control: 15%. Stakeholder acceptance and documentation: 5%. Total: 100%. KPI-based payment calculation For each payment component: Payable amount = Work Package value × component weight × performance factor. KPI target fully achieved: Performance factor 100%. Minor shortfall; no material operational impact and corrective action accepted: Performance factor 90%. Moderate shortfall or repeated minor non-conformity: Performance factor 75%. Material shortfall affecting service quality, but deliverable remains usable: Performance factor 50%. Critical acceptance criterion not met: Performance factor 0%; payment withheld pending remediation. Payment for each deliverable shall equal the deliverable value multiplied by the weighted achievement of its applicable KPI components. Amounts associated with remediable shortfalls shall be withheld and may be released following corrective action and successful re-verification within the agreed cure period. Failure to meet a mandatory acceptance criterion shall result in withholding of the affected component until acceptance is achieved. Critical criteria — such as operational availability, completion of daily readiness checks, correct escalation of critical incidents, post-maintenance functional testing, security compliance and configuration control — are to be treated as mandatory gates. For recurring Work Packages, monthly payment with quarterly reconciliation will be used: 80% of the monthly Work Package value: paid following acceptance of the monthly operational, maintenance and CSI evidence. 15% performance retention: released quarterly based on aggregated KPI achievement. 5% final retention: released at Work Package closure following completion of outstanding actions, records, documentation and handover. For short, milestone-based Work Packages: 20% upon approval of the Work Package plan, baseline and readiness arrangements. 60% upon completion of the operational, maintenance or improvement activities and achievement of the principal KPIs. 20% upon final acceptance, including reporting, documentation, corrective-action closure and handover. 7. PENALTIES AND INCENTIVES Any penalties are subject to contract discussions. 8. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS NATO security policy compliance. Valid security clearance required. Qualified and experienced personnel. English language proficiency. Stable team with minimal rotation. Purchaser approval for personnel changes. Proper handling of PFE equipment. Use of ITSM system mandatory. Immediate escalation of blocking issues. End-user impact must be minimized. 9. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE The Service will be delivered in Mons, Belgium in a typical office environment designated as a Class II Security Area. No travel required. 10. SCHEDULE The BASE period of performance is September 1, 2026 (tentative) and will end December 31, 2026. If the 2027 option is exercised, the period of performance is January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2027. If the 2028 option is exercised, the period of performance is January 1, 2028 to December 31, 2028. 11. SECURITY The security classification of the service will be up to NATO SECRET, preferable in progress of upgrade to NATO Cosmic Top Secret. The contractor providing the services under this SOW is required to hold a valid CTS clearance (NATO SECRET security clearance is accepted with CTS in progress – deadline to have CTS in place by end of October 2026). 12. QUALIFICATIONS [See Requirements] 11. SECURITY The contractor providing the services under this SOW is required to hold a valid NATO COSMIC TOP SECRET clearance (NATO SECRET security clearance is accepted with CTS in progress – deadline to have CTS in place by end of October 2026). 12. QUALIFICATIONS Education A Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field is preferred. title: Vice President, Salesforce Product Management (Belgium)
description: Shape the future of how the world's biggest Salesforce teams build, protect, and innovate. Location: Remote (US) / Pleasanton, CA Reports to: Chief Executive Officer Why This Role Matters Every day, the world's most mission-critical companies — banks, hospitals, governments, and Fortune 500 enterprises — run on Salesforce. And every day, the teams behind those orgs face a choice: move fast or stay safe. At Flosum, we refuse that tradeoff. As the only 100% Salesforce-native DevSecOps, data, and security platform, we empower teams to ship fearlessly, recover instantly, and govern with confidence — all without leaving the platform they love. We're looking for a visionary product leader who sees what's possible when innovation and trust live in the same place. Someone who wants to leave a fingerprint on an entire ecosystem. The Opportunity This is more than a product role — it's a chance to architect the operating system for the modern Salesforce enterprise. You will own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for a platform that touches release managers at sunrise, developers at midnight, and CISOs every minute in between. You'll lead a passionate team of product managers, partner shoulder-to-shoulder with brilliant engineers, and sit at the table with customers solving problems that matter — from accelerating releases by 10x to recovering an org in minutes after a catastrophic event. If you've ever wanted to build the category-defining product in Salesforce DevOps, this is your moment. What You'll Do Set the North Star. Craft a bold, multi-year product vision that anticipates where Salesforce — and the AI-powered enterprise — is heading next, from Agentforce to Data Cloud and beyond. Build the team that builds the future. Recruit, mentor, and inspire a world-class product organization across DevOps, data management, and security — a team people fight to join and never want to leave. Obsess over customers. Sit with admins, developers, release managers, and security leaders. Understand their 2 a.m. anxieties and their 10 a.m. ambitions. Turn those insights into products they'll champion. Ship things that matter. Drive the full lifecycle — from messy whiteboard to flawless launch — for capabilities like Git-based version control, AI-assisted code review, intelligent backup & recovery, and zero-trust security. Stay ahead of the platform. Turn every Salesforce release into an opportunity, not a fire drill, ensuring Flosum is always first and always native. Win the category. Outthink and outmaneuver every competitor by knowing the market deeper than anyone else and telling a story only Flosum can tell. Be a force multiplier. Partner with marketing, sales, success, and AppExchange & SI partners to turn great products into great businesses. Who You Are A product leader with 10+ years of experience and the scars and wins to prove it — including 3+ years building and leading PM teams. A Salesforce native at heart — you dream in metadata, you've debugged a deployment at midnight, and you know why governor limits exist (and how to live with them). A builder who has shipped DevOps, ALM, data protection, or security products that customers genuinely love. A strategist who can paint the 5-year picture and an operator who can ship next Tuesday. A storyteller comfortable in front of a single customer, a packed room, an analyst, or a board. A magnet for talent and a champion of the people you lead. Bonus Superpowers Deep fluency in Git, CI/CD (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps), and modern developer workflows. Experience with backup, archival, sandbox seeding, and data masking at enterprise scale. Battle-tested in regulated environments — SOC 2, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR. A point of view on how AI will reshape the Salesforce admin and developer experience — and the chops to ship it. Salesforce certifications, an engineering background, or an MBA that sharpens your edge. What Success Looks Like One year from now, you will have published a roadmap the entire ecosystem talks about, built a team that's the envy of the industry, and shipped releases that move ARR, expand customer relationships, and cement Flosum as the undisputed leader on the AppExchange. Five years from now, you'll look back at a category you helped define — and an enterprise software movement you helped lead. If you're ready to do the most meaningful work of your career, we're ready to build it with you.

title: Azure Cloud Platform Engineer (Ghent)
description: D-ploy is an IT and Engineering Solutions company delivering services to organizations across the EMEA region and the United States. We work closely with our clients to provide reliable, secure and practical technology solutions, supported by collaborative teams and a people-focused working environment. We are looking for an experienced Azure Cloud Engineer to join a cloud platform environment supporting a global organization in the pharmaceutical sector. In this role, you will help build, automate and operate cloud infrastructure and shared platform services used by different business and technology teams. You will work primarily within Microsoft Azure , with a strong focus on Infrastructure as Code, Terraform, Kubernetes and DevOps automation . You will collaborate with cloud architects, application and data teams, platform specialists and external partners to deliver cloud solutions that are secure, scalable and aligned with governance and compliance requirements. Your responsibilities will include: Designing, deploying and maintaining Azure infrastructure using Terraform and Infrastructure as Code principles. Supporting a broad range of Azure services across compute, networking, storage, identity, security and monitoring. Creating reusable infrastructure components, automation frameworks and standard cloud deployment patterns. Supporting application and workload teams as they onboard services to the organization's cloud platforms. Operating and maintaining shared cloud platform capabilities and ensuring they remain stable, available and performant. Supporting and troubleshooting containerized workloads running on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) . Contributing to platform upgrades, lifecycle activities and ongoing technical improvements. Managing GitHub repositories and supporting branching, pull-request and source-control practices. Building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines used for infrastructure and platform deployments. Identifying opportunities to automate manual processes and improve consistency across the cloud environment. Applying cloud security standards and supporting governance requirements around monitoring, tagging, cost management and compliance. Supporting audit and compliance-related activities within a regulated environment. Working closely with architects, application teams, data teams and external partners on cloud solution design and implementation. Creating and maintaining technical documentation and operational procedures. Sharing knowledge and contributing to engineering standards and best practices across the cloud platform team. At least 3 years of professional experience in Cloud Engineering, Platform Engineering, DevOps Engineering or a similar role. Strong hands-on experience working with Microsoft Azure in enterprise environments. Solid knowledge of Terraform and Infrastructure as Code practices. Practical experience with Kubernetes , ideally Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) . Experience designing, deploying and supporting cloud infrastructure in complex organizational environments. Good understanding of cloud-native architectures and modern platform engineering approaches. Strong knowledge of Azure networking concepts such as Virtual Networks, Private Endpoints, DNS, load balancing, Network Security Groups and firewalls . Familiarity with cloud security, identity and monitoring solutions. Experience working with GitHub, source control and CI/CD processes . Previous experience supporting Kubernetes-based platforms and containerized applications. Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills with a practical approach to problem solving. An automation-focused mindset and the ability to identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency. Strong communication and documentation skills. Ability to work effectively with multiple technical teams and stakeholders. Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. Valid criminal record extract, not older than three months, required. Nice to have: Experience with AWS in addition to Azure. Previous experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare or another regulated industry. Experience working within a platform engineering or internal cloud services team. Exposure to different workload types, including application, integration, data or AI platforms. Relevant technical certifications such as Microsoft Azure Administrator (AZ-104), Azure Solutions Architect (AZ-305), Terraform Associate or Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) .

title: CDT-0022 Engagement and Communications Consultant (NS) - WED 2 Sep
description: Deadline Date: Wednesday 2 September 2026 Requirement: Engagement and Communications Consultant Location: NATO Headquarters in Brussels, BE Full Time On-Site: Yes Total Scope of the request (hours): 500 hrs. (Estimate) Required Start Date: As soon as possible End Contract Date: 31 December 2026 Required Security Clearance: NATO SECRET Special Terms and Conditions: The contractor will be responsible for complying with the respective national requirements for working permits, visas, taxes, social security etc. whilst working on site at NATO HQ Brussels, Belgium. No special status is either conferred or implied by the host organisation, NATO HQ Brussels, Belgium to the contractor whilst working on site. The contractor will be responsible for complying with all the respective National Health regulations in Belgium before taking up the position. 1. INTRODUCTION The Cyber and Digital Transformation Division (CDT) leads NATO's digital transformation, cybersecurity and cyber defence efforts, translating NATO priorities into coherent strategies and coordinated delivery across the Alliance to strengthen interoperability, resilience, cybersecurity and operational effectiveness. The Division seeks a consultant to strengthen its engagement with industry, academia, NATO stakeholders and Allied public. The consultant will develop and implement targeted outreach, communications and activities that enhance the Division's agenda in implementing Cyber and Digital Transformation for the Alliance. Working as part of the coherence team, and closely with other section heads and directors, and supporting the division's leadership and relevant NATO communications, policy and technical stakeholders, the consultant will translate complex cyber and digital transformation topics into clear, compelling and audience-appropriate messages. 2. TASKS Prepare high-quality communications products, including speeches for leadership, key messages, presentations, briefing materials, web and social-media content, stakeholder packages and event-related materials. Develop and maintain an engagement and communications plan for industry, academia, Allied stakeholders and relevant public audiences in order to raise awareness and understanding of cyber, AI and data, and hybrid issues, and CDT developments in these areas. Develop a strategic narrative to link CDT efforts in training, exercises, concept development and policy documents. Identify, map and describe priority relationships with digital and cyber technology companies, defence industry, research institutions, think tanks and professional networks. Support the planning and delivery of conferences, workshops, roundtables, bilateral engagements and public-facing activities, including speaker preparation, audience targeting and follow-up, in cooperation - and with advice - from the Office of Strategic Communication. Advise leadership on strategic positioning, stakeholder perceptions, communications opportunities and reputational risks, and provide regular reporting on outreach activities and results. 3. PROFILE [See Requirements] 4. LOCATION OF DUTY The service will be executed on-site at the NATO HQ offices in Brussels, Belgium, no teleworking permitted. Limited travels to other NATO bodies and Committee meetings in NATO Countries may be required. 5. TIMELINES The services of the contractor are required for the period starting as soon as possible until 31st December 2026. Possible extension of the contract in 2027 and 2028. Contract extensions are subject to performance of the contractor, budget availability and related NATO regulations. 6. REPORTING & SPECIFIC WORKING CONDITIONS The contractor will be embedded as part of the coherence team and reports to the DASG Strategy and Policy. The contractor shall comply with all general rules, terms, and conditions applicable to working within the CDT at NATO HQ Brussels. This includes security protocols, data protection guidelines, and any specific operational procedures. 7. LINK TO CDT OBJECTIVES This work will ensure that CDT has a structured and strategic stakeholder engagement Framework that is aligned with the division's priorities. Objective O1: Develop a stakeholder engagement Roadmap. KPI: Complete and validated stakeholder mapping and engagement strategy. Timeline: Within 3 months. Objective O2: Build stakeholder relationships. KPI: Identify and categorised 100% of key internal and external stakeholders by influence, interest and engagement level. Timeline: End of 6th Month. Objective O3: Develop communication material for the leadership as requested. KPI: Speaking notes and presentation material are available 2 days before the event. Timeline: Ad-hoc and as requested by senior leadership. 8. TRAVEL Occasional business travel may be required. Travel expenses will be reimbursed to the individual directly (in addition to the hourly rate) under NATO rules. Travel to Shape will not be reimbursed. 9. SECURITY AND NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT The contractor must be in possession of a NATO SECRET security clearance before being considered as a candidate. A signed Non-Disclosure Agreement will be required. 3. PROFILE The candidate holds a university degree in communications, marketing, public relations, political science, international relations, security studies, technology policy or another relevant discipline. The candidate has demonstrated senior experience (8+ years) in strategic communication, stakeholder engagement, public affairs, marketing or external relations, preferably in the cyber, digital, defence, security or emerging-technology sectors. The candidate has 3 years of experience in a senior or lead communications role, advising management and leading strategic communication initiatives. The candidate has strong knowledge of NATO's internal structures, decision-making processes, stakeholder environment and civil-military working practices, gained through relevant professional experience. The candidate has excellent written and spoken English (SLP 4/4/4/4), with the ability to communicate complex technical and policy issues clearly to senior officials, specialist audiences and the public. The candidate must possess a valid NATO security clearance required for the assignment. 9. SECURITY AND NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT The contractor must be in possession of a NATO SECRET security clearance before being considered as a candidate. A signed Non-Disclosure Agreement will be required.

title: 2026-0105 NELDOM Orchestration & Role Mapping Delivery Service (NS) - FRI 21 Aug
description: BIDDING INSTRUCTIONS Technical Proposal Bidders shall submit a proposal clearly providing the following information: Understanding and experience within NATO More than 7 years of NATO experience related to Education and Training. Previous experience at the NATO HQ and across the NATO Enterprise performing digital transformation related stakeholder engagement, strategy planning and operational execution. Track record of collaboration with NETFs and the Bi-Strategic Commands (BiSCs) in the field of NATO L&D. Proficiency in the NATO Joint Exercise Management Module (JEMM) and the NATO Training Objective Management Module (TOMM). Application experience of the NATO Lessons Learned process (for the purpose of quality assurance). Highly experienced in NATO Individual and Collective training and exercises within National and NATO frameworks. This includes the creation of TNAs and L&D solutions for consumption by NATO Enterprise personnel. Industry and Professional Experience More than 7 years industry experience in change management and L&D-related posts. Master's degree in Communications, Public Relations, Security related field, and/or multi-year experience in a role conducting Digital Transformation in an international environment. Prior experience in the creation and delivery of L&D offerings in all formats (residential, online, distributed, hybrid) to international organizations such as NATO, UN, etc. Technical skills and certifications Must possess an internationally recognized Cybersecurity certification. Certification in ITIL 4 and Agile Project Management. Approach on deliverables and execution Ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment. Significant experience in event management, and the planning, design and delivery of NATO L&D exercises and training events. Demonstrated ability to deliver learning architectures/experiences and skills-competency mappings using the Skills for the Information Age (SFIA) and the National Initiative for Cybersecurity Education (NICE) frameworks. Experience of designing enterprise-level Operating Models. Experience of design and delivery of engagement strategies and maturity models aligned to NATO cybersecurity and ICT coherence objectives. Deadline Date: Friday 21 August 2026 Requirement: NELDOM Orchestration and Role Mapping Delivery Service Location: 10% on-site & 90% Offsite Period of Performance: 2026 BASE: 15 September 2026 until 31 December 2026 2027 Option: 1 January 2027 until 31 December 2027 2028 Option: 1 January 2028 until 31 December 2028 Required Security Clearance: NATO SECRET 1. SERVICE NAME NELDOM Orchestration and Role Mapping Delivery Service 2. STRATEGIC CONTEXT The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) is seeking a NATO Enterprise Learning & Development Operational Model (NELDOM) Orchestration Delivery Service (NODS) to provide support to the development and implementation of Enterprise-wide Learning and Development (L&D) strategies for CDT Division Cyber Readiness initiatives and more specifically for the NELDOM project. This service will focus on ensuring positive user experience and driving engagement across the Individual to Collective Education and Training (E&T) spectrum throughout the NATO Enterprise by coordinating and conducting Orchestration engagements with NATO stakeholders, both through face-to-face and virtual engagements. The NODS will support local commanders and working level staff articulate gaps and priorities in order to aggregate them, and, in turn, raise awareness of other entity's gaps and priorities in order to achieve improved cybersecurity posture and hygiene for their organizations through an uplift in the capabilities of their workforce via a range of L&D activities conducted via innovative formats and technologies. The NODS will work closely with the NELDOM Project team, NCIA Project Manager, Learning designers, developers, and L&D communities of interest throughout the NATO Enterprise to build user-centric L&D experiences that align with the CDT Division Cyber Readiness function. This encompasses the comprehensive assessment, oversight, and implementation of enterprise-wide capabilities and initiatives, all geared towards the realization of NATO's Digital Transformation in support of NATO 2030 objectives through more coordinated L&D efforts, as well as enabling the NELDOM project Team to more rapidly engage with NATO Enterprise entities in order to aggregate local entity information into a more accurate and effective NELDOM design and execution. 3. KEY FOCAL POINTS The 2026 Service Delivery focuses on advancing NATO's L&D ecosystem from Phase 0: Assembly through Phase 1: Building Communities of Interest (CoIs) and into Phase 2: Developing Communities of Understanding (CoUs). The service will support the design, implementation, and operationalisation of the NELDOM, ensuring systematic progression of four target communities toward mature Communities of Practice (CoPs). The 2026 deliverables are structured to: Establish functional CoIs through voluntary governance, shared frameworks, and best effort initiatives. Transform CoIs into CoUs through formalized governance, shared frameworks, and pilot initiatives. Support the design and implementation of NELDOM governance structure, processes, and integration architecture. Establish NATO Enterprise-wide coordination infrastructure supporting cross-community collaboration. Prepare foundations for Phase 3: CoPs Transition in 2027 & 2028. 4. OPERATIONAL CONTEXT 2025 Achievements Foundation The 2025 L&D Mobile Engagement Delivery Service (MEDS) successfully completed Phase 0 activities including: Comprehensive stakeholder mapping across NATO Education and Training Facilities (NETF), Human Resources (HR), Bi-Strategic Commands (Bi-SCs), and DIANA, Industry and Academia (DIA) communities. Value proposition development demonstrating collaboration benefits. Initial governance framework documentation. Strategic engagement with 40+ NATO Enterprise entities. Proof-of-concept collaborations (ICT Role Mapping, NATO entity partnership). 2026 Strategic Priorities The 2026 service extension addresses critical transformation requirements: Operationalise NELDOM as the integrating framework for NATO Enterprise L&D activities. Transition communities from informal interest groups to structured understanding networks. Establish systematic knowledge transfer mechanisms between communities. Formalise governance structures through Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs). Facilitate the launch of pilot initiatives within the CoIs demonstrating tangible collaboration value. 5. SCOPE OF WORK Objective The NODS provider will be responsible for coordinating the design and delivery of NATO Enterprise-wide L&D initiatives and post-activity analysis to ensure that they are consumed effectively by a broad spectrum of NATO Enterprise stakeholders. This will incorporate the development and implementation of blended learning activities and rapid engagement strategies that align with NCI Agency and CDT initiatives in support of the NELDOM. This service will also involve conducting user research; formulating the design and delivery of distributed L&D offerings (residential/ mobile/ hybrid); creating user journey maps; tracking and analysing comprehensive L&D engagement metrics; and managing stakeholder relationships while contributing to the definition of the broad spectrum of NATO L&D initiatives especially related to the linkages between Individual and Collective learning practices. It is expected that the incumbent will have to engage consistently with centres of excellence (eg: CCDCOE), NATO Education & Training Facilities (NETFs), namely the NCI Academy, NATO School Oberammergau and NATO Defence College, and HQ Supreme Allied Command Transformation (SACT). 6. KEY ACTIVITIES User Research and Journey Mapping Conduct quarterly user research to understand user needs and pain points related to the L&D mobile engagement. Create Enterprise personas and user journey maps to identify opportunities for improving the mobile user experience. Design and Delivery of L&D Offerings Conduct bespoke Training Needs Analyses (TNAs) for respective training audiences (technical and non-technical). Formulate the design and delivery of L&D solutions to appropriately address the TNAs. Employment of Learning Management Systems. Engagement Strategy Within the remit of the NELDOM scope develop and implement L&D engagement strategies, engagement plans and communication plans that align with CDT initiatives. Collaborate with designers, developers, and product managers to create user-friendly learning experiences. Effectively lead, manage and deliver simultaneous projects, ensuring all projects meet their requirements and are delivered on time, to cost and quality standards, while realising any identified benefits. Create and manage project milestones; critical learning pathways; and potential risks and issues, ensuring that appropriate and effective mitigation strategies and contingency plans are prepared. Metrics Tracking and Analysis Track and analyse bespoke metrics to measure the success of mobile engagement and initiatives. Identify areas for improvement and make recommendations based on data analysis. Change Management Develop a change management plan to support the adoption of CDT initiatives through mobile channels. Identify and address potential resistance to change from mobile users. Stakeholder Management Within the remit of the NELDOM scope identify key stakeholders across the NATO Enterprise who will be impacted by or influence CDT initiatives. Develop and maintain relationships with stakeholders to ensure alignment and buy-in. Communicate effectively with stakeholders to keep them informed of project progress and address any concerns. Conduct institutional analysis and quality assurance reporting directly to senior NATO Enterprise leadership. Content Management On a monthly rotation adapt at least four compelling content artefacts for internal stakeholders via communication channels, including newsletters, intranet, and other platforms. Within the remit of the NELDOM collaborate with at least 10 different NATO Enterprise entities to ensure consistency and alignment with CDT organizational messaging. On a weekly basis, review and contribute to the creation of digital content, ensuring information flow is up-to-date and user-friendly. On a bi-monthly basis review and update implementation strategies to improve content curation, enabling better engagement and accessibility across the NATO Enterprise. Collaboration Within the remit of the NELDOM scope engage daily with NCI Academy and CDT L&D staff and project teams to actively support L&D portfolio delivery. Leadership & Employee Engagement On a monthly rotation support the planning and execution of internal events, workshops, and employee development programs. Within the remit of the NELDOM scope design and support the preparation of engagement and key leadership development, ensuring alignment with the overall CDT communication strategy. Support the dissemination of important updates and messages from leadership to staff. Feedback and Analysis Establish feedback mechanisms to assess the effectiveness of internal communications. Within the remit of the NELDOM scope design and analyse NATO Enterprise-wide engagement metrics to evaluate engagement and make recommendations for improvement. Due to the AGILE approach of this project, there is a need to define a set of specific arrangements between NCIA and CDT and the contractor that specifically defines the deliverables to be provided as well as their associated acceptance criteria. This includes deliverable planning, execution and review processes, which are detailed below. NELDOM Design and Implementation Support the design of comprehensive NELDOM governance architecture defining roles, responsibilities, processes, and decision-making authorities. Support the development of a NELDOM integration framework connecting NATO Enterprise L&D entities. Support the creation of a NELDOM service catalogue defining standardized NATO L&D offerings. Support the establishment of a NELDOM metrics framework measuring enterprise-wide L&D effectiveness. Facilitate NELDOM validation through stakeholder workshops and governance board reviews. Community Maturation Coordination Within the remit of the NELDOM scope conduct quarterly Community Maturity Model (CMM) assessments measuring progress against defined criteria. Facilitate vision-setting workshops establishing shared objectives and success metrics. Coordinate development of shared taxonomies, frameworks, and standards. Support pilot initiative design, implementation, and evaluation. Manage Memoranda of Understanding (MoU) development and signature processes. Knowledge Management and Transfer Design and implement knowledge repositories for each NELDOM community. Establish cross-community knowledge exchange mechanisms. Create documentation standards and templates. Facilitate Lessons Identified/ Lessons Learned (LI/ LL) capture and dissemination using the NATO LI/ LL format and best practices. Support best practice identification and sharing. Metrics, Analysis, and Reporting Within the remit of the NELDOM scope develop comprehensive metrics frameworks measuring community maturity progression. Track engagement metrics, participation rates, and collaboration intensity. Conduct quarterly stakeholder satisfaction assessments. Analyse pilot initiative outcomes and value realisation. Produce executive-level progress reports and recommendations. Stakeholder Engagement and Change Management Within the remit of the NELDOM scope execute targeted stakeholder engagement strategies for each community. Facilitate periodic community forums building relationships and trust. Conduct change impact assessments and mitigation planning. Develop communication strategies ensuring consistent messaging. Manage resistance through targeted interventions and stakeholder dialogue. Planning Objective: Plan the objectives for the upcoming quadrimesterly block. Kick-off meeting: Conduct a kick-off meeting at the beginning of each quadrimesterly block to plan the objectives and deliverables as described in Section 7 (Deliverables and Payment Milestones). Agree on the required level of effort: Determine the necessary level of effort for each task within the quadrimester and allocate resources accordingly. Deliverable Strategy & Rollout Plan: Develop and update the Orchestration Delivery Strategy & Rollout Plan and the Quadrimester Performance Monitoring Matrix (QPMM) at the beginning of each quadrimester (Months 1, 5, and 9). Execution Objective: Within the remit of the NELDOM scope execute the agreed plans with continuous monitoring and adjustments. Bi-Monthly Deliverables: The contractor will produce and deliver bi-monthly reports as specified in the deliverables section (e.g., combined reports on engagements, Quadrimester Rollout Progress Reports (QPRRs)). Regular Meetings: Conduct regular meetings between the NCIA, CDT and the contractor to review progress, address issues, and make necessary adjustments to the processes or production methodology. Meetings will be held physically in the office or in loco. Progress Tracking: The contractor will use a shared dashboard or tool to track the status of the deliveries and any issues. Quality Assurance/ Quality Check: The contractor shall ensure that the quality standards agreed for the deliverables are maintained throughout the quadrimester. title: C005071 Solution Engineer (SATCOM) (NS) - FRI 21 Aug
description: Deadline Date: Friday 21 August 2026 Requirement: Solution Engineer (SATCOM) Location: Braine-l'Alleud, BE Full Time On-Site: Yes Time On-Site: 100% Total Scope of the request (hours): 600 Required Start Date: 28 September 2026 End Contract Date: 31 December 2026 Required Security Clearance: NATO SECRET Duties & Role: Solution architecture Provide technical lead support to acquisition projects, ensuring the delivery of integrated and interoperable technical solutions, preparing technical specifications, supporting evaluation processes, ensuring technical leadership throughout the implementation process and supervising acceptance testing; Contributes to the development of solution architectures in specific business, infrastructure or functional areas. Identifies and evaluates alternative architectures and the trade-offs in cost, performance and scalability. Determines and documents architecturally significant decisions. Supports projects or change initiatives through the preparation of technical plans and application of design principles. Aligns solutions with enterprise and solution architecturestandards (including security). Reviews requirements for errors and omissions. Prioritises requirements and documents traceability to source. Provides input to the requirements base-line. Investigates, manages and applies authorised requests for changes to base-lined requirements, in line with change management policy. Systems development management Plans and drives systems development projects which support the organisation's objectives and plans. Ensures projects are carried out in accordance with agreed architectures, standards, methods and tools and addresses security and privacy requirements. Sourcing Prepares pre-qualification questionnaires and tender invitations in response to business cases. Recognises the difference between open source and proprietary systems options. Applies standard procedures and tools to produce detailed evaluation criteria for complex tenders and to evaluate tenders. Contract management Acts as a routine contact point between the organisation and suppliers concerning contract management. Systems design alternatives evaluation Oversees System design reviews Ensures that the system design balances functional and non- functional requirements. Reviews systems design and ensures that appropriate methods, tools and techniques are applied effectively. Makes recommendations and assesses and manages associated risks. Systems integration, test and acceptance Plans and drives activities to develop organisational systems integration and build capabilities including automation and continuous integration. Identifies, evaluates and manages the adoption of tools, techniques and processes to create a robust integration framework. Provides authoritative advice and guidance on any aspect of systems integration, test and acceptance. Responsible for overseeing all integration activities to ensure they align with the agreed system and service designs Assesses risks and takes preventative action. Measures and monitors applications of standards. Knowledge and engineering experience in state-of-the-art technologies, across a broad spectrum, which should include Deployable CIS, Infrastructure as a Service and familiarity with related international / commercial / industrial standards; Knowledge and experience in System Engineering; Knowledge and experience in applying MBSE methodology; Knowledge and experience in applying ITIL principles and methodology applied to effective Service Management and Control; Prior experience of working in an international environment comprising both military and civilian elements; Knowledge of NATO responsibilities and organization, including ACO and ACT. Understanding of NATO operational standards, procedures, and communication protocols; Knowledge and experience with SATCOM operations, engineering support, or related defence communication systems; Strong analytical capability applied to system performance, interoperability, and technical assessment activities. International recognized System Engineering training or certification International recognized MBSE training or certification ITIL v4 foundations

title: Security Engineer - Node.js Proactive Defense (worldwide remote, work anywhere)
description: CloudLinux is a global remote-first company. We are driven by our principles: do the right thing, employees first, we are remote first, and we deliver high-volume, low-cost Linux infrastructure and security products that help companies to increase the efficiency of their operations. Every person on our team supports each other and does what we can to ensure we all are successful. Check out our website for more information https://cloudlinux.com/ Imunify360 Security Suite is a product of CloudLinux Inc., the maker of the #1 OS in security and stability for hosting providers. Imunify is an innovative security solution designed specifically for shared and VPS/Dedicated servers. The automated, easy-to-use solution with the six-layer approach to security delivers comprehensive and complete attack prevention. The mission We protect web hosting providers and the sites running on their infrastructure through a defense-in-depth stack: web-server-layer WAF, runtime application self-protection for PHP, deep application integrations (WordPress plugins and similar), a malware scanner with cleanup capability, and network-layer firewalls and IP reputation. The pieces talk to each other, and the threat intelligence they generate at scale powers detection across the stack. Node.js is the segment of the hosting market growing fastest, and the next layer we want to build for it is runtime protection inside the Node.js process itself. Most Node.js workloads on managed hosting today are AI-generated web apps deployed by non-technical owners who can't, won't, and shouldn't be expected to patch their own code or audit their own dependencies. We're going to defend those apps anyway — at runtime, without their cooperation, without breaking them. You'll build that runtime protection layer end-to-end. What you'll own The product. A brand-new product line, yours to define — what we intercept, what we don't, what the customer-visible surface looks like. The technical approach. Instrumentation strategy, deployment shape, programming language — all open. You'll consult with our architects but the direction is yours. Implementation, end to end. You'll have the full tooling stack we provide — LLM subscriptions, modern dev infrastructure, the works. Use what makes you fast. Methodology. How you build conviction in your detection logic — your call. Cross-layer signal. Our existing stack produces threat intelligence at unmatched scale: tens of millions of monitored sites, petabyte-scale malware sample storage, real-time domain and URL reputation, IP-level attack feeds. These are available for you to plug into. Use what helps. How we'll measure success The product is held to four numbers: runtime overhead, false positives, false negatives, and customer-escalation volume. They reflect what hosting providers and their customers care about. Hit them well and the product runs inside a meaningful slice of the modern Node.js web. What we're looking for An experienced researcher or engineer who can build and iterate on a brand-new product, driving both the research and the development. The hard part of this work is knowing what's malicious, what's vulnerable, and what's just an unusual but legitimate pattern — and being right about it across the long tail of frameworks, libraries, and customer code we'll encounter in production. Must have: Proven experience building and shipping a new product, security solution, major feature, or technical system from scratch. Strong evidence of end-to-end technical ownership, from initial investigation and architecture through implementation, release, and production iteration. Strong web application security knowledge and current knowledge of practical exploitation. A working sense of how detection rules behave at scale — what catches attackers without flagging the long tail of legitimate code. Ability to start as the PM, architect, lead engineer, and QA for this product. You ask for resources or help when you need them; you don't wait to be told what to do. Comfort directing AI coding agents to high-quality output. Nice to have: Prior work on runtime-protection products, application firewalls, or instrumentation tooling. Background in malware analysis or incident response. Familiarity with managed-hosting environments. Public security research, vulnerability disclosures, or detection rulesets you've authored. Familiarity with the Node.js runtime and the JavaScript ecosystem. What it's not Not a scope-and-handoff role — you drive the work and own the outcome. Not a "platform team will productize this later" role — you ship to real customer fleets and watch the telemetry quickly. Not a spec-and-review role — you are hands-on every day. Why this matters Most managed-hosting customers are not developers. They cannot patch their apps. They cannot audit their dependencies. They will keep deploying vulnerable code from AI assistants because that's how modern web apps get built now. The textbook advice — "secure your code, audit your dependencies" — does not apply to them. If we don't intercept exploits at runtime, nobody will. The numbers you hit on detection, performance, and false positives will materially affect how much of the modern web stays online when the next exploit class drops.

Proficiency in scripting, automation, troubleshooting, and the implementation and configuration of enterprise security controls and cybersecurity monitoring solutions. Hands-on experience administering, integrating, and optimizing Splunk Enterprise, Splunk Enterprise Security, Splunk SOAR, Splunk UBA, and Cribl Stream platforms, including data ingestion pipelines and lifecycle management. Experience developing, testing, and fine-tuning SIEM correlation rules, detection logic, automated playbooks, and security orchestration workflows, leveraging MITRE ATT&CK and D3FEND methodologies. Experience applying Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and CI/CD practices using Azure DevOps to deploy, configure, and manage security platforms and monitoring infrastructure. Experience designing and implementing security monitoring capabilities and architectures, including High-Level Designs (HLDs), Low-Level Designs (LLDs), technical blueprints, security monitoring use cases, and supporting technical documentation. Strong technical writing and communication skills, including the development of technical reports, security policies and procedures, business cases, cybersecurity roadmaps, executive presentations, and the evaluation of cybersecurity technologies, MSSPs, and strategic security initiatives. Very good command of English (minimum B2 level). Eligibility to obtain an EU Personal Security Clearance, at a later stage is required.

From executive roadmapping to production-ready systems and workforce upskilling, Ajaia embeds intelligent tools directly into the workflows that matter most. Mission: Help organizations win the AI moment. Position Overview Ajaia is hiring a Cloud Security & DevOps Engineer to manage and secure the company's multi-cloud infrastructure across GCP and Azure. This is a technical, hands-on role. You will configure infrastructure, enforce security controls, manage deployment pipelines, and build automation that reduces manual overhead across IT and security operations. The company operates AI products across regulated industries, so you will support compliance requirements (HIPAA, SOC 2) at the infrastructure level. You are expected to think about security as part of every system you build or maintain, not as an afterthought. Internal IT operations (access management, endpoint security, onboarding automation) are also part of your scope. The company is AI-first. You should already be using AI tools to write scripts, analyze logs, generate documentation, and accelerate your engineering work. We expect candidates to use AI in daily workflows across research, ideation, drafting, design iteration, quality checks, and delivery acceleration. AI fluency is a core execution requirement, not optional tooling. similar) Experience building and securing CI/CD pipelines Working knowledge of cloud security fundamentals: IAM policies, network segmentation, firewall rules, encryption at rest and in transit title: IT Infrastructure Administrator
description: Role Purpose The IT Infrastructure Administrator owns the design, deployment, and ongoing operation of Omilia's core IT infrastructure — spanning on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments. The role ensures the reliability, security, and scalability of network, server, and cloud systems that underpin Omilia's internal operations and platform delivery, acting as the primary technical owner for infrastructure health and capacity. Accountabilities Owns the availability, performance, and security posture of Omilia's IT infrastructure across network, server, and cloud layers. Accountable for infrastructure lifecycle management: capacity planning, procurement, deployment, maintenance, and decommissioning. Responsible for backup integrity, disaster recovery readiness, and business continuity across all managed systems. Ensures infrastructure compliance with Omilia's security policies and relevant certifications (ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI-DSS). Contributes to infrastructure strategy and roadmap, identifying opportunities to improve resilience, efficiency, and cost. Key Responsibilities Administer and maintain network infrastructure: LAN/WAN, firewalls, VPN, DNS, DHCP, and switching/routing equipment. Manage server infrastructure (physical and virtual) including provisioning, patching, performance tuning, and decommissioning. Administer cloud infrastructure across GCP, AWS, or Azure: compute, storage, networking, and IAM configurations. Manage virtualisation platforms (VMware, Hyper-V) and containerisation environments where applicable. Implement and maintain backup and disaster recovery solutions; conduct periodic DR tests and document outcomes. Monitor infrastructure health using observability tools (e.g. Zabbix, Datadog, Grafana); respond to and resolve infrastructure incidents. Enforce infrastructure security controls: patch management, vulnerability remediation, access hardening, and certificate management. Manage on-premises and cloud storage solutions, ensuring data integrity, retention compliance, and performance. Maintain infrastructure documentation: network diagrams, runbooks, configuration baselines, and change records. Support IT security audits and contribute infrastructure evidence to compliance programmes (ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI-DSS). Knowledge, Skills & Experience Required: 3–5 years of IT infrastructure administration or systems engineering experience. Hands-on experience with network administration: firewalls (e.g. Fortinet, Palo Alto, Cisco), VPN, DNS/DHCP, VLANs. Solid experience with server administration on Linux and/or Windows Server environments. Experience with at least one major cloud platform (GCP, AWS, or Azure) at an administration level. Experience with virtualisation technologies (VMware vSphere, Hyper-V, or equivalent). Familiarity with backup and DR tools and methodologies; experience designing or testing recovery procedures. Knowledge of infrastructure security principles: hardening, patch management, access controls, certificate lifecycle. Experience with infrastructure monitoring and alerting tools. Methodical approach to documentation, change management, and incident response. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; able to diagnose complex infrastructure issues under pressure. Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Network Engineering, or a related field. Nice to have: Relevant certifications: CCNA, CompTIA Network+, AWS/GCP/Azure Associate, VMware VCP, or equivalent. Experience with infrastructure-as-code tools (Terraform, Ansible, or similar). Exposure to containerisation and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes). Experience in a SaaS, cloud-native, or CCaaS technology environment. Omilia Note - Contribute actively and effectively as an integrated team member. - Act as an Omilia ambassador in all interactions.

title: Information Security Engineer
description: About the Opportunity Dentons Europe is currently seeking a Information Security Engineer, specializing in Microsoft cloud technologies to play a key role in strengthening and evolving our security landscape. In this role, you will design and implement security controls across cloud and hybrid environments, with a strong focus on Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Azure. You will operate at the intersection of architecture and execution shaping security decisions, guiding technical teams, and ensuring that systems, applications, and integrations meet the firm’s security, compliance, and reliability standards. As a trusted advisor and technical authority, you will work closely with Information Security, IT, and business stakeholders across Europe, embedding security into the design and delivery of technology solutions while continuously improving the organization’s overall security posture. This is an opportunity to make a visible, enterprise-wide impact in a complex, international environment. You will primarily be accountable for Design, implement, and maintain robust security and compliance controls across Microsoft 365, Microsoft Azure, and hybrid environments. Act as a cybersecurity subject-matter expert for Europe and Country IT teams providing clear, practical guidance on secure design and implementation. Assist in embedding security into application, infrastructure, identity, endpoint, and integration architectures (including APIs and data flows), ensuring alignment with secure development lifecycle practices and architectural standards. Collaborate with architects, engineers, project teams, and business stakeholders to define security requirements as integral part of enterprise initiatives and technology solutions from the outset. Work closely with SOC and CSIRT teams to support incident response activities, including investigation, containment, and remediation, and ensure lessons learned are reflected in improved controls and architecture. Lead end-to-end vulnerability management activities, including vulnerability scanning, assessments, penetration testing coordination, and remediation tracking with system owners and technical teams. Identify, assess, and mitigate security risks across cloud and enterprise environments, driving measurable improvements in the firm’s security posture. Provide advanced troubleshooting and technical leadership for complex or high-impact security issues. Develop and maintain security documentation, standards, reports, and control frameworks. Minimum 3 years of experience in cloud security or enterprise cybersecurity engineering Advanced expertise in Microsoft Azure security, including at least two of: Defender for Cloud Microsoft Sentinel Infrastructure / Network Security (IaaS) Application and API security Storage and database security Advanced expertise in Microsoft 365 security, including at least two of: Microsoft Entra ID, identity and access management Microsoft Purview, data protection and compliance Microsoft 365 Defender suite Intune / Endpoint Manager Strong understanding of: Security architecture principles, including Zero Trust, defense-in-depth and least privilege Hybrid cloud environments and system integrations Vulnerability management, including analyzing penetration testing and coordinating remediation of results API security and modern integration technologies Scripting and automation skills, e.g., PowerShell, Python or Bash Strong interest in security architecture, with a desire to deepen exposure and grow toward architectural responsibilities Professional experience Proven experience designing and implementing secure solutions in Microsoft technologies-based enterprise environments Experience working with large-scale or multi-country IT environments Solid exposure to security operations, incident response and security tooling Experience collaborating across infrastructure, development and business teams

title: Test specialist with interest in IT and Pension
description: Are you a Test Specialist with a passion for technology and a strong and numerical and international mindset? Would you like to use your skills in an international organization where quality, data and technology go hand in hand? Then you might be the colleague we are looking for. As a Test Specialist at Keylane, you will work with our core pension platform called Plexus and play an important role in ensuring the quality and reliability of our solutions. You will contribute to optimizing the solution for existing customers as well as supporting implementations for new clients. Your work will have a direct impact on the quality of our product. By combining your testing expertise with strong analytical skills, you will help ensure that we build the right solutions from the outset and identify and resolve defects early in the development process. Key about your role You will: Perform regression testing of core pension functionality, including underlying calculations, across customers and products. Investigate deviations and test results, analyse the underlying data and calculations, and provide clear and accurate insights that help the team identify root causes and resolve issues. Test new features and functionality to ensure they meet both functional requirements and expected business outcomes. Provide pension calculations and testing. Identify opportunities to improve both our product and the way we test it. Contribute ideas and initiatives related to test automation and the use of AI in testing. Take an active role in our ongoing test improvement programme and help strengthen our overall approach to quality assurance. Key about your team You are part of our new Customer Support and Operation (CSO) department together with many driven and experienced colleagues. As a part of the CSO department, You will join the Release Management team, a group dedicated to ensuring the smooth delivery of our pension software releases to customers. The team is responsible for testing and verifying that each release is ready for deployment. You work in a team composed of various expertise (pension-related, actuarial, technical) in which you support our Product Development teams, project teams and the customers. You will work in a mixed team, i.e. with the local Dutch, Danish and Indian team, each with their own expertise. We are looking for someone who enjoys working with complex systems, data and calculations and thrives on collaborating across international teams. Ideally, you have: An educational background in in math, IT or a related field. At least +3 years experience in software testing or data analysis. Experience with or knowledge of the pension industry – this is a strong advantage. Experience with SQL or are comfortable working with databases and data analysis. Have a hands-on mindset, take ownership and are comfortable driving tasks and issues forward. Strong numerical and analytical skills, as many of the tasks involve working extensively with data and calculations. Communicate confidently in both Danish and English. Other information Please send your application with CV via our website. Applications are evaluated continuously. Each employee within Keylane must follow training on information security and irrespective to the role basic information security responsibilities apply.
